title: A ceiling on knowledge-building media
statement: Set a ceiling on the share of a reading lesson given to knowledge-building film and audio, and measure that share on the built lesson.
example: One built lesson played 5:13 of film and audio before the first line of the text itself.
detail: A build map of a live Grade 9 lesson, read from the build on 8 October 2026, measured 5:13 of film and audio before the first line of the play: an introduction (27.6 s), the unit film (208.5 s) and a first part that is a prose summary (77.1 s) (`g9/library/text/L25efa0.txt`, lines 33-34). Notes from a planning call the same day record a directive to establish clear media ratios, with a cap on knowledge-building media at 30%–40% as the example, so that lessons stay structured around core reading competencies (`g9/library/text/L612555.txt`, line 144). The 30%–40% figure is that example, not a tested value.
against: The unit film's brief gives that media a knowledge job of its own: "The world, the people, the kind of story and the words students need." (`g9/library/text/Lbde498.txt`, line 12).

evidence.quote: 5:13 of film and audio come before the first line of the play
the introduction (27.6 s), the unit film (208.5 s) and part 1 (77.1 s), which is a prose summary, not the play.

the team must establish clear media ratios (e.g., capping knowledge-building media at 30%–40%) so that lessons remain structured around core reading competencies and scale efficiently across the curriculum
